targets.text: associate ships an accuracy method (issue #20): every tool call in a run carries a purpose the model stated before it ran and a harness-written record of what was asked, what was sent, how it ended and what came back; every fact the model reports cites the walk entry it came from and quotes that entry's saved result word for word, and a deterministic matcher in the harness checks each quote; conclusions carry the numbered facts they rest on and name their source kind (file read, tool call, agent conclusion, memory, web); and each run reports countable accuracy — how many facts and claims were made, checked, passed and refused, per kind — so an operator can follow any answer link by link back to saved results without re-running anything
every sentence of the announcement is demonstrated by a live worker run and a live cortex run on pi 1.5.2 whose walk, facts file and counts are kept; until then the docs say built and unit-tested

the operator can see, for any run, exactly why each tool was called, every piece of evidence collected, and what conclusions were made, with each item labelled by its source kind (file read, tool call, agent conclusion, memory, web) — operator's request of 2026-11-17 on issue #20

given only a run export directory, a reader can list for every call its purpose, its outcome and its saved result, and for every fact its source kind, without re-running anything and without reading the model answer
accuracy is calculable by count: the number of each fact and each claim a run made, and how many of each were checked, passed and refused — operator, 2026-11-17
the counts are produced by the Python harness from the saved files, equal a hand count on a recorded run, and never include an unchecked fact in passed
associate itself, on the worker and cortex models, is used for live testing and for review of real work on this change — operator, 2026-11-17
the delivery records live worker and cortex runs with their session ids, and at least one review of a real change made by an associate run, each as a single run and not a rate

every tool call carries a purpose the model states before the call (the question it settles and what it expects to see); a call with no purpose is refused in the tool_call hook before it runs, and the harness copies the purpose into the walk entry

a call with a missing or empty purpose is refused before it runs for every tool in models.json tool_names except finish and associate_ready, write and edit included, and the refusal text says how to add one; shown by a hook-level test per tool and one live run

the walk entry is the harness-written record of an action: purpose, arguments as asked, arguments as sent, how it ended with a reason, and a pointer to the full saved result with a count of what the model was not shown

for a recorded call the entry shows the arguments as the model gave them and as the tool used them, differing when the tool ignored or defaulted one (the 2026-11-17 read with limit and offset is a test case), and names a saved file that holds the whole result with the number of characters the model was not shown
the walk stays harness-written: a purpose is model-authored text that the harness copies from the call it received, and no tool or model can write a walk line directly
no code path lets a tool or the model append a walk line; the purpose in an entry is byte-equal to the purpose argument of the call the hook received (after redaction)
every refusal and failure a model receives carries a reason and how to fix the request; a non-ok outcome without a reason is a harness bug
a test enumerates every refusal constructor in guard.ts, gate.ts, contain.ts and the tools and fails if one can produce a refusal without a reason or without a fix

a fact is a value, the walk entry it came from, and a quote of that entry's saved result word for word; the harness checks each quote with a deterministic matcher against the saved result, one fact at a time, refuses a quote that is not there and shows the nearest match, and marks a fact from a source it cannot read as unchecked

the matcher is deterministic (same inputs, same verdict, no model call); a fact whose quote is absent from the cited saved result is refused with the nearest matching span; one bad fact does not refuse the others in the same hand-back; a fact citing an entry with no saved text is marked unchecked
the prose hand-back route drops walk ids that the walk never recorded, as the finish route already does, so an invented [wN] marker can no longer make a statement count as referenced
a final message citing [w999] in a three-entry run is recorded as unreferenced; this test fails on the current code
the model can run the quote check during the run through a tool that uses the same matcher the harness uses to grade the result afterwards
the tool and the post-run check call the same matcher implementation in the extension, and the Python matcher returns the same verdict on every shared test vector under associate/contract/

no runtime dependency is added: the matcher uses the Python standard library on the harness side and Node built-ins in the extension, and thresholds, retry rounds and view sizes live in associate/contract/, never as TypeScript literals
pyproject.toml dependencies stays [] and package.json declares no dependency; rounds, view sizes and matcher settings are read from associate/contract/ and grep of the extension finds no literal copy

every walk entry carries a source kind set by the harness from the tool that produced it (file read, tool or command output, web, memory, agent conclusion, harness measurement), every fact inherits the kind and the known limits (truncated, stale) of the entry it cites, and a closing conclusion backed only by an agent conclusion or memory is refused

the kind is derived from the tool name by a table in the contract, never from model text; a conclusion whose only support is a spawn_subagent hand-back, a delegate_status final_reply or an eidetic_recall result is refused as a closing conclusion, while delegate_status harness fields (outcome, merge, tests) count as first-hand

finish becomes an enforcing check: a hand-back whose facts fail the quote check, or whose conclusion rests on something unread, is refused with what is wrong and how to fix it; the model answers again in the same session for a fixed number of rounds set in the contract; after that the run ends with a named failure reason and no result is reported as accepted

a refused finish leaves the session able to call tools again; the round limit comes from the contract; after the last round the run result names the failure and nothing reports the hand-back as accepted

a conclusion is recorded apart from observations and explanations: alternatives are listed with what each predicts and what would refute it, each ends supported, refuted or open with the numbered facts it rests on, an open one names the check that would decide it, and "cannot tell" is an accepted answer

the finish payload schema carries alternatives, verdicts and open items; a supported or refuted verdict with a non-empty list of unread items is refused; an open item with no deciding check is refused; a hand-back whose answer is cannot-tell with a named check is accepted

each run reports a count per kind next to its result: facts made, checked, passed, refused and unchecked; conclusions supported, refuted and open; statements with no fact; by source kind — written by the harness, never by the model; the harness also stores its own reviewer flags (an unbacked link, a conclusion resting on something unread) beside the result without changing it, in a file an outside grader can add to
the counts and flags are written to a file beside the hand-back by the harness; the hand-back file is byte-identical before and after flags are added
each new check names the measured failure that motivated it, so a check can be removed when its reason no longer holds
each check in the contract carries a motivating-failure field naming a recorded run or document, and a test fails when one is missing
a ledger entry that claims a result cites the walk entry that measured it and the harness checks that the entry exists; the harness can append the measured outcome itself (issue #15)
a ledger_append whose refs name a walk id that does not exist is refused with the fix; this depends on the ledger binary being installed, which it is not on the survey machine today
eidetic-cli is not changed: a remembered fact carries its walk reference and quote in the free-form metadata the store already round-trips, and the freshness signal is not used as a staleness marker
no file in eidetic-cli changes; a record written by eidetic_remember carries the session id, walk id and quote in metadata and they come back unchanged on recall
lobes-cli and colleague are not changed, and no checkpoint id enters the contract, prompts or docs
git diff over lobes-cli and colleague is empty for this work, and grep finds no checkpoint id in models.json, culture.yaml, prompts or docs
the model-stated purpose is recorded and shown to the operator but is not added to the state the safety gate scores, so gate.json stays at version 9 for this work
the state posted to the decider is byte-identical with and without a purpose on the call, gate.json version stays 9, and a test asserts the purpose key is absent from the gate arguments
every tool result the model is shown is stamped by the harness with its walk id, so a fact cites an id the model was given instead of one it counted
every tool result text the model receives begins with a harness line naming its walk id; shown by a test over every tool and by a live run where 100% of results carry their id
live runs are kept able to continue and their reasoning is controlled by the operator; where associate cannot do either, colleague (which is resumable) is used instead — operator, 2026-11-17
the delivery states for each live run its reasoning setting and whether it was a continuation; associate gains no per-run reasoning flag in this spec (that is a follow-up issue)

a fact names its source unambiguously across runs: a reference to an entry of a prior run loaded with --continue-from, or of a child run, is distinguishable from an entry of the current run and resolves to that run's saved result

in a run started with --continue-from, a reference to a prior-run entry is written in a form that cannot equal a current-run id, resolves to the prior export, and the 2026-11-17 case (22 prior ids resolved against the new walk) is a failing-then-passing test
the harness pin moves from pi 1.1.0 to pi 1.5.2 as part of this work (operator decision, 2026-11-17: upgrading to 1.5.2 is approved)

the extension test suite passes on pi 1.5.2, docs/notes records a verdict for each breaking change between 1.1.0 and 1.5.2, and the pin changes in associate/harness/pi.py only after a live run on 1.5.2 is recorded; pi-acp is re-checked against 1.5.2 or its status is stated
the operator who reads a run's result to decide whether to trust it, and the next agent (a mesh peer, a parent cortex, or a continued run) that builds on that result without re-running it
the result is usable by both readers from files alone: a person following links by hand and a program reading the JSON

a finished run hands back, beside its answer, a walk in which every action has a stated purpose and a harness-written record, a list of facts each tied to one walk entry by a quote the harness matched, conclusions that name the facts they rest on, and a count of what was made, checked, passed, refused and left unchecked; a hand-back that fails the check is refused in session and, if still failing, ends the run with a named reason
each element named in the after state exists as a file or field in the export of a recorded live run

today a statement is free text with optional walk ids the model was never shown; the harness checks only that an id exists and that a cited line fell inside a read range; nothing is refused; a false sentence and a true one carry the same label; and a run killed at its time limit returns nothing
each statement of the before state is backed by a scope finding citing code or a 2026-11-17 run (s9, s11, s28, s29, s30)

a reader cannot tell a checked sentence from an invented one in today's hand-back: on 2026-11-17 cortex reported a table in a file it never read, worker and cortex cited walk entries that were not the ones they meant and were still marked referenced, and the share of referenced statements did not track which answers were correct
the three failures cited are in recorded runs scope20-cortex-t1, scope20-worker-t2 and scope20-worker-t5, whose walks are kept with the delivery or their loss is stated

on a fixed set of at least 5 read or find tasks with hand-checked answers, run live on worker and on cortex, every fact reported as passed is found word for word in the saved result of the entry it cites when re-checked by the Python harness (0 mismatches), and the harness's counts equal a hand count of the same hand-backs
the task set and hand-checked answers are committed before the measuring runs; results are reported as counts per run, not as a rate

replaying the 2026-11-17 failures as tests, 4 of 4 are caught: an invented [w999] id in a final message, a fact quoting text absent from the cited entry, an id of a prior run cited in a continued run, and a call made with no purpose
each of the four replays is a test that fails on the code at commit 33141ff and passes after the change

no free text reaches the caller as a checked answer: the answer in the run result is rendered by the harness from the accepted facts and conclusions, and whatever else the model wrote (the finish summary, the final message) is delivered under an unchecked label with its sentence count in the report

the answer field of the run result is produced by harness code from accepted items only; a test feeds a hand-back whose summary contains a sentence no fact supports and the sentence appears only under the unchecked label and in the uncovered count
a statement that an action happened (a tool ran, a file changed, a test passed, a record was stored) is a fact whose cited entry must be a call of that tool that did not end in an error or refusal
a fact saying a tool succeeded that cites an entry of another tool, or an entry ending in an error or refusal, is refused with the fix; the t20 A2 case is the test

two further recorded failures are replayed as tests and 2 of 2 are caught: the cortex sentence about pyproject.toml carried in a finish summary (scope20-cortex-t1), and the senses report of "Eidetic remember: Success" with no eidetic_remember call (t20 run A2)
both replays are tests that fail on the code at commit 33141ff and pass after the change

a passed fact means its quote is in the saved result of the entry it cites; it does not mean the value is true or follows from the quote. Reports name the count quote-checked, and the word accuracy is used only for results on the hand-checked task set
no report, doc or CLI text of this work calls the quote-checked count accuracy; the word appears only next to results on the hand-checked task set
the matcher refuses a quote shorter than a minimum length set in the contract, and when a fact value is a literal (a number, an identifier, a path) that literal must occur inside the quote
the minimum length is read from the contract; a fact with a literal value absent from its quote is refused; both have a test with a passing and a failing case

the checks ship with a mode set in the contract, report or enforce, per model and overridable per run: in report mode nothing is refused and the report says what would have been; a model moves to enforce only after a recorded live run in report mode

the mode is read from the contract; in report mode a hand-back that would be refused is accepted and the report lists the refusals it would have made; the default for every model is report until a live run is recorded

consecutive refusals for the same reason (a missing purpose, a failed hand-back) are capped by a number in the contract; at the cap the run ends with a named outcome instead of looping to its time limit
a test drives the same refusal past the cap and the run ends with the named outcome; the cap is a contract value

the extension writes the facts, the check results and the counts itself in every session, so mesh sessions through pi-acp and spawned children have them; the Python re-check runs wherever associate run runs (headless and delegated runs), and the report says when it did not run

a session started without associate run (the extension loaded directly) leaves the facts, check results and counts files in its export; the report carries a field saying whether the Python re-check ran

an export says which format it is: the checker, the counts and --continue-from accept an export written before this change and report its facts as not applicable instead of failing; the stub adapter writes the new shape
a pre-change export fixture is accepted by the checker, by walkstats and by --continue-from without an error; the stub adapter output validates against the new schemas
a fact names its source by run label and walk id only, validated by pattern; the harness maps that to a saved file, and neither the matcher nor the check tool opens a path supplied by the model
the reference pattern admits no path separator; a test passes a reference containing a path and it is refused before any file is opened
the same checks apply to senses; the delivery includes at least 1 live senses run under them or states that senses is unmeasured
the delivery names the senses run by session id, or says in the same place that senses was not measured

acceptance_criteria: associate/contract/accuracy.json exists with a version and these keys: mode per model (report or enforce, every model report), retry rounds, refusal cap, minimum quote length, a source-kind table keyed by tool name, the purpose-exempt tools (finish, associate_ready), and a checks list where each check has an id, a strength and a motivating_failure
associate/contract/schemas/ gains accuracy.schema.json, facts.schema.json and report.schema.json; contract.SCHEMA_NAMES and validate.py cover them; a test fails when a check has no motivating_failure
the extension loads accuracy.json through lib/contract.ts (ASSOCIATE_CONTRACT_DIR honoured) and a node test asserts no setting from it appears as a literal in the extension
pyproject.toml dependencies is still [] and package.json declares no dependency (asserted by a test)
tasks.instruction: Own associate/contract/accuracy.json, the three new schema files, associate/contract/__init__.py, associate/contract/validate.py, .pi/extensions/associate/lib/contract.ts and their tests. The facts schema defines a fact as id, value, source reference, quote, and an optional action flag; the report schema defines the per-kind counts, per-source-kind counts, the flags list and a field saying whether the Python re-check ran. Reference form for a source: an optional run label then a walk id, no path characters. Every later task reads these files, so keep names stable once merged.

the commit that adds it precedes any measuring run (stated in the file header with the commit it was checked against)

acceptance_criteria: associate/contract/matcher_vectors.json holds cases covering: exact match, whitespace and read line-stamp differences, a quote absent (with the expected nearest span), a quote shorter than the minimum, a literal value missing from its quote, and a source with no saved text (unchecked)

a new .pi/extensions/associate/lib/results.ts saves each result text in full under the session export up to caps.max_raw_chars, one file per walk id; above the cap the entry is marked partial

the entry is still written once, when the result arrives, by the recorder only: a test asserts tools and model text have no path to append a line and that the stored purpose equals the purpose on the call after redaction
an entry written from a call with no purpose (an exempt tool, or a pre-change fixture) validates; existing walk tests pass or are updated in this task

Read the purpose from the call arguments the recorder already remembers (noteToolCall); read args-as-used from the result details key the tools task will fill (define the key name here and document it in walk.ts). Saved results are the redacted text, as today. Do not touch index.ts.

a closing conclusion supported only by agent-conclusion or memory entries is refused; delegate_status harness fields count as first-hand; a supported or refuted verdict with unread items is refused; an open item with no deciding check is refused; cannot tell with a named check is accepted

index.ts is edited by t7 (tool_call handler), t9 (tool_result path) and t11 (finish tool) in three successive waves, and walk.ts by t6 then t9; the waves keep them serial, and each task names the part of the file it owns.

pi 1.5.2 docs: "An unknown tool or invalid arguments skip `tool_call`". A call pi rejects for its arguments never reaches the hook, so the walk has no entry for it and the refusal text is pi's, not ours; it shows only as tool_execution_end with an error. Consequences: purpose must stay optional in every schema and be enforced in the hook (t7, t8); recording such calls in the walk is not in any task and would need a deviation (candidate owner t9, which holds the result path of index.ts).

The rule that tools cannot write walk lines is enforced by types and a source scan only: ctx.walk() returns the whole recorder object at run time, because the narrowing to ChildWalkLinker is type-only (reported by the t6 builder). A runtime limit needs a change in lib/runtime.ts, which no task owns.

Entries for calls pi rejected before the hook (deviation d1) usually have empty args: in pi 1.5.2 tool_execution_end carries no args, only tool_execution_start does (reported by the t9 builder from pi's bundle). Those results are also not stamped with a walk id, because pi offers no hook to change them.

associate check reads only the current run: it does not load a prior run or child walks, so a fact citing prior:wN or cN:wN is not re-checked by the Python side even though check_handback supports it (reported by the t16 builder).
The bridge on main (associate runs show, the HTTP API, the web UI) does not surface handback_outcome or the accuracy counts, and reports a run that exited 3 only as "the run exited with 3".
